workflows.name: Image to Textured 3D Model
workflows.description: Generate a 3D mesh from a single image and paint it, end to end, using Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2 shape and paint pipelines (kijai's ComfyUI-Hunyuan3DWrapper). Unlike three-d.texture-mesh, which expects an already-generated GLB and produced no visible texture on the raw marching-cubes output it was given, this workflow generates the mesh and textures it in the same graph: the freshly generated shape is cleaned up (floater/degenerate-face removal, face count reduction) before UV-unwrapping and multi-view texture painting, which is what the raw output was missing. Use this when you want a textured model from an image in one pass; use three-d.texture-mesh only if you already have a clean, UV-mapped mesh from elsewhere.

inputs.description: Image used both to generate the mesh's shape and to paint its texture

inputs.label: Max face count
inputs.description: Mesh is reduced to at most this many faces before UV-wrapping and texturing

inputs.label: Delight steps
inputs.description: Steps used to strip existing lighting/shadows from the reference image

workflows.name: Texture Mesh From Image
workflows.description: Paint a texture onto an existing 3D mesh from a single reference image, using Tencent's Hunyuan3D-2 paint pipeline (kijai's ComfyUI-Hunyuan3DWrapper). The mesh is UV-unwrapped if needed, rendered from six camera angles to get normal and position maps, the reference image is "delighted" (its baked-in lighting removed) and used to condition a multi-view diffusion model, and the generated views are baked back onto the mesh's UV texture and gap-filled before export as a textured GLB. Newly installed on this machine: the custom-node package and its CUDA rasterizer extension had to be compiled from source against ROCm/HIP, since it only ships prebuilt wheels for Windows+CUDA. Requires a ComfyUI restart to pick up the newly installed custom node before this pack will run.

workflows.name: SCAIL-2 Character Replacement (Wan 2.1)
workflows.description: Rebuilt from scail2MultiRefSegmented_v6.json - despite living in this suite's image-editing staging pile, inspecting its actual node graph shows it's a WAN 2.1 video pipeline, not an image editor: driving-video + reference-image character replacement via zai-org's SCAIL-2 model (SAM3 subject tracking + colored-mask identity binding + WanSCAILToVideo conditioning), wrapped in an elaborate Chinese-language "WAN ANI Director" multi-segment queue UI. Those Director/"SQR" nodes (WanAniDirector, SQRSCAIL2TransitionToVideo, SQRScail2ReferenceBatchSplit, SQRScail2ColoredMaskAdvanced, WanSQRMultiReference, WanContextWindowsManual) come from the public zere111ai/ComfyUI-WanAni-SQR repo and exist purely to auto-chunk arbitrarily long videos into overlapping segments and stitch them back together - convenience automation, not the core capability. The actual generation core (WanSCAILToVideo, SCAIL2ColoredMask, SAM3_VideoTrack) turned out to already be native ComfyUI nodes in this install (comfy_extras/nodes_scail.py, nodes_sam3.py), so this pack reproduces ComfyUI's own bundled reference template (video_wan21_scail2_character_replacement.json) instead, trimmed to a single segment/pass (the source's "Base" subgraph; the segment-chaining "Extend" subgraph and the Director's shot-auto-detection were dropped as out of scope for one pack). Of the model list in that template's own notes: umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors, Wan2_1_VAE_bf16.safetensors, sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors, and the lightx2v_I2V_14B_480p_cfg_step_distill_rank64_bf16.safetensors LoRA were all already installed in this suite under those exact names - no substitution needed. The SCAIL-2 base diffusion model itself (wan2.1_14B_SCAIL_2_fp16.safetensors), the DPO refinement LoRA (wan2.1_SCAIL_2_DPO_lora_bf16.safetensors), and clip_vision_h.safetensors are NOT installed under any name in this suite (the staged workflow's own DiffusionModelLoaderKJ pointed at a differently-named int8 quant of the same base model that also isn't present) - all three are flagged below with the official template's own Hugging Face links rather than guessed at or downloaded. Marked experimental until those three land.

workflows.name: LTX-2.3 Director (GGUF Image-to-Video)
workflows.description: Hand-built from the Q8 GGUF-quantized LTX-2.3 22B diffusion model (ltx219BAllYouNeedIs_ltx2Q80GGUF.gguf, from the "All You Need Is..." pack) plus the node graph in ComfyUI's own official "Image to Video (LTX-2.3)" blueprint (repos/ComfyUI/blueprints/), rather than importing the "LTX2.3 All-In-One SFW/NSFW LTX Director" zip verbatim. That zip contains three exports - LTX23Legacy.json (a pre-Director, manual-timeline-segment editor), LTX23LTXDirector2.json (its own Quick-Start note calls this "a hot-fix to make the new version of the LTX Director work with this workflow, so not all the new features are available or tested"), and LTX23LTXDirector13.json (the current, fully-updated Director build, superseding Director2). All three are ~300-500 node mega-templates wiring in a dozen optional side chains (ControlNet preprocessing via comfyui_controlnet_aux, RIFE frame interpolation, MelBandRoFormer voice separation, Nvidia RTX super-resolution, pysssss UI scripts, easy-use pipe nodes) behind rgthree mute/bypass groups - reproducing that exactly would mean installing 6+ more custom node repos of uncertain provenance for features orthogonal to the core video pipeline, so this pack instead wires a clean minimal single-pass T2V/I2V graph using core ComfyUI's native LTXV nodes (added upstream for LTX-2.3 support) plus the GGUF loader. A separate standalone export, videoflowLTX23AllInOneT2VI2VA2V_ltx23AllInOneV30.json, was checked against the zip's contents and is NOT a duplicate - its subgraph names ("Stage 1/2 Sampler", "TalkVid ID-LoRA", "Voice Separation") show it's a different third-party "VideoFlow" two-stage-upscale template with talking-head identity LoRA and voice isolation, an even larger and more specialized undertaking; it was left unpacked here as out of scope for this pass. Sampling parameters (9-step manual sigma schedule, euler_ancestral_cfg_pp, cfg 1) are taken from the blueprint's final (non-distilled/"dev") decode stage, applied here as a single pass at target resolution instead of the blueprint's base-res-then-spatial-upscale two-stage flow, since the ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.1.safetensors upscaler model isn't installed either. The GGUF supplies only the quantized diffusion transformer; the video VAE and the "LTXAVTextEncoderLoader" CLIP wrapper both need the full ltx-2.3-22b-dev-fp8.safetensors checkpoint (Lightricks/LTX-2.3-fp8 on Hugging Face, ~29GB) which is NOT installed in this suite and was not downloaded - both are flagged with url below. The Gemma-3 12B text encoder side of that wrapper IS covered by the already-installed gemma_3_12B_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors. The bleach-bypass i2v LoRA (a photochemical high-contrast, desaturated color-grading look - the same benign style family as this suite's SD1.5/SDXL bleach-bypass LoRAs) is wired in as an optional-strength LoraLoaderModelOnly slot on the GGUF model. Needs the city96/ComfyUI-GGUF custom node for the UnetLoaderGGUF node (already installed in this suite by the time this pack was built). Marked experimental: without the ltx-2.3-22b-dev-fp8.safetensors checkpoint this graph cannot actually decode a video end to end.

inputs.default: cinematic tracking shot, smooth natural motion, coherent detail, high production value

inputs.label: Negative prompt
inputs.default: low quality, worst quality, deformed, distorted, disfigured, motion smear, motion artifacts, jittery, static frame

workflows.name: Wan 2.2 Long-Video 6-Step GGUF Combo (SVI, 4-Clip Chain)
workflows.description: Imported from a user-authored ComfyUI export (wan22I2vWorkflowForLONGVideos_v30.zip / i2v_WAN22_6step_3Samplers_GGUF_Combo_SVI_v2.json), preserved as-is: a "Stable Video Infinity" (SVI) long-video technique built on Wan 2.2 14B I2V, where up to 4 clips are generated in sequence, each one starting from the last frame of the previous clip (via ImageFromBatch + VAEEncode), then optionally upscaled (RealESRGAN-family model + downscale-by), interpolated (RIFE) up to a target frame rate, and finally concatenated (VHS_VideoCombine) into progressively longer combined videos. Each clip runs a 2- or 3-KSamplerAdvanced chain (toggled by a "Use 2 Samplers?" boolean and an rgthree Fast Groups Bypasser on the "Step 2" group) whose total step count is split across samplers by SimpleMath+ nodes, and the whole thing can switch between regular .safetensors UNETLoaders and quantized UnetLoaderGGUF/ CLIPLoaderGGUF nodes via a "Use GGUF Models?" boolean plus LazySwitchKJ routing - hence "6-step GGUF Combo" in the source filename. The non-GGUF fallback UNETLoaders pointed at a community "Dasiwa" merge (DasiwaWAN22I2V14BV8V1_midnightflirtHigh/LowV7.safetensors) that isn't installed here, but the workflow's own embedded "Models to download!" note says explicitly "choose your favourite, this is what I've been using" and lists wan2.2_i2v_high/low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors as the documented base models - so these were repointed to this suite's installed copies of exactly those files rather than left missing. The installed CLIPLoader/VAELoader targets (umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors, wan_2.1_vae.safetensors) already matched the source graph exactly - no changes needed there either. Several models genuinely have no local equivalent and are left pointing at their original filenames with download urls (mostly lifted directly from the workflow's own embedded documentation note, which is unusually thorough): the two GGUF UNETs (DasiwaWAN22I2V14BTastysinV8_q8High/Low.gguf, a Civitai community GGUF quantization of the same Dasiwa merge - noted here, but a generic non-community alternative also exists at QuantStack/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-GGUF on HuggingFace if the Civitai model is ever taken down), the GGUF CLIP loader's umt5-xxl-encoder-Q8_0.gguf (city96/umt5-xxl-encoder-gguf), the two "SVI_v2_PRO_Wan2.2-I2V-A14B_HIGH/LOW_lora_rank_128_fp16.safetensors" LoRAs that this long-video technique is actually named after and depends on for its per-clip continuity (Kijai/WanVideo_comfy, under LoRAs/Stable-Video-Infinity/v2.0/) - these are required for the SVI behavior itself, not optional - the "remacri_original.pth" upscale model used in the (bypassable) upscale stage of each clip, and the "rife49.pth" RIFE checkpoint used in the (also bypassable) interpolation stage. The lightning LoRA used in the optional "Step 2" pass of each clip (wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_high_noise.safetensors) was already installed under that exact name - no change needed, though it ships disabled (on: false) in the source graph by default. Beyond core ComfyUI, this graph needs ComfyUI-GGUF (UnetLoaderGGUF/CLIPLoaderGGUF), ComfyUI-KJNodes (LazySwitchKJ, INTConstant/BOOLConstant, ImageResizeKJv2, ImageBatchMulti, ImageBatchExtendWithOverlap, WanImageToVideoSVIPro), rgthree-comfy (Power Lora Loader, Reroute, Bookmark, Fast Groups Bypasser), ComfyUI_essentials (SimpleMath+, BatchCount+), cg-use-everywhere (Anything Everywhere - used pervasively instead of direct links to broadcast the loaders/prompts/settings to all 4 clip groups), ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation (RIFE VFI), ComfyUI-Image-Saver (Width/Height Literal), and ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite (VHS_VideoCombine) - none of the first six were installed in this suite, so they were cloned from their well-known upstream GitHub repos, matching the approach used for the other imported packs in this batch.

workflows.name: JibMix Wan V3 SeeMe (Text-to-Video)
workflows.description: jibMixWan_v3SeeMe.safetensors was found loose in this suite's staging folder with no accompanying workflow, so it wasn't clear what kind of Wan checkpoint it was or how it should be wired up. Its safetensors header identifies it as a single 14B-scale Wan diffusion UNET (40 transformer blocks, 5120-dim, matching Wan 14B, not the 1.3B/30-block/1536-dim variant), stored fp8_e4m3fn (no scale_weight tensors, so it's a plain fp8 cast rather than ComfyUI's "_scaled" fp8 format) - its embedded metadata even includes the ComfyUI graph that produced it, a bare UNETLoader -> ModelSave pair that re-saved "Jib_Mix_Wan_V3_A_00001_.safetensors" as this file, consistent with "JibMix" being a merged/finetuned checkpoint (in the tradition of the SD/SDXL "JibMix" merge line) rather than an official Wan release. Critically, its patch_embedding.weight is [5120, 16, 1, 2, 2] (16 input channels) and it has no img/k_img/v_img cross-attention tensors and no vace_blocks - i.e. it's architecturally a plain T2V UNET, not the 36-channel I2V architecture (compare wan2.1_i2v_480p_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors, which has a 36-channel patch embedding plus per-block k_img/v_img tensors) and not a VACE-patched checkpoint either (compare the wan2.1_vace_1.3B/14B checkpoints referenced by this suite's causvid packs). So despite living in the wan21ImageToVideo_v30.zip staging bundle, it is not a safe drop-in for an I2V (WanImageToVideo-with-start_image) or VACE (WanVaceToVideo) pipeline. It was moved to models/diffusion_models/jibMixWan_v3SeeMe.safetensors and given this minimal from-scratch text-to-video workflow instead: UNETLoader -> ModelSamplingSD3 -> KSampler, conditioned by two CLIPTextEncode nodes off the installed umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors text encoder, with WanImageToVideo used purely as an empty-latent generator (its start_image input is left unconnected, which the node's own code path treats as plain text-to-video - it only builds the 36-channel image-conditioning concat when an image is supplied), decoded with the installed wan_2.1_vae.safetensors and packaged into an MP4 via the core CreateVideo/SaveVideo nodes. All models referenced here are already installed; no substitutions or missing dependencies. This pack uses only core ComfyUI nodes.

workflows.name: Wan 2.1 VACE 14B + CausVid (Reference-to-Video)
workflows.description: Imported from a user-authored ComfyUI export (wan21ImageToVideo_v30.zip / wan-vace-causvid-tomgoodnoise/wan-vace-causvid-14b-tomgoodnoise.json), preserved as-is: the 14B variant of the official ComfyUI "Wan Vace Reference to Video" template workflow, higher quality than the 1.3B version and (per the workflow's own note) capable of 720p in addition to 480p. Same structure as this suite's video.wan21-vace-causvid-1.3b pack - a single reference image plus a text prompt through WanVaceToVideo, accelerated with Kijai's extracted 14B CausVid LoRA (2-4 step distillation instead of the default 20 steps/cfg 6.0), followed by RIFE frame interpolation from 16fps to 32fps. Per readme.txt in the source zip, this technique and workflow originate from Tom Goodnoise (tomgoodnoise.de). The UNETLoader points at wan2.1_vace_14B_fp16.safetensors and the LoraLoader at Wan21_CausVid_14B_T2V_lora_rank32.safetensors - neither is installed in this suite (this is a VACE-patched checkpoint, architecturally distinct from the plain T2V/I2V Wan 2.1 checkpoints already installed here, so there's no safe local substitute) - both are left pointing at their original filenames with download urls taken directly from the workflow's own embedded documentation notes. workflows.name: Wan 2.1 VACE - Character + Background Composite
workflows.description: Modified from this suite's video.wan21-vace-causvid-1.3b (the official ComfyUI "Wan Vace Reference to Video" template) to take two images into one generation instead of one. The stock template only wires WanVaceToVideo's reference_image input (a single subject/identity image, VAE-encoded separately and never itself a video frame). This pack additionally loads a background image, repeats it across every frame (RepeatImageBatch, count kept in sync with the Frames widget via a shared primitive), and feeds that into WanVaceToVideo's control_video input, which the stock template leaves unconnected. With control_masks left unconnected, VACE defaults that mask to all-ones, meaning the whole control_video is treated as a loose generation guide rather than a locked, untouched plate - so the model composites the reference character into the given background and animates it, instead of either ignoring the background or pasting the character over a frozen still. This is the correct native VACE mechanism for combining a subject and a scene in a single pass, as opposed to storyboard-style approaches (start/end frame, keyframe-to-video) that generate sequential frames rather than simultaneous elements. Same model stack as video.wan21-vace-causvid-1.3b (Wan 2.1 VACE 1.3B + Kijai's CausVid distillation LoRA + RIFE 16fps->32fps interpolation) and the same substitutions apply: UNETLoader/LoraLoader point at wan2.1_vace_1.3B_fp16.safetensors and Wan21_CausVid_bidirect2_T2V_1_3B_lora_rank32.safetensors, neither installed in this suite (left pointing at their original filenames with download urls); CLIPLoader repointed to the installed umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors (the template's own notes say fp16 or fp8 both work); VAELoader (wan_2.1_vae.safetensors) was already installed under that exact name. Swap in the 14B UNETLoader/LoraLoader pair (see video.wan21-vace-causvid-14b for the exact names/urls) for higher quality at the cost of speed and VRAM - the two extra nodes added here don't care which VACE checkpoint size is loaded. Negative prompt has a few extra terms discouraging background drift; raise WanVaceToVideo's strength widget if the result invents too much new background instead of respecting the one you gave it. Marked experimental until the two core models are installed under those exact names.

workflows.name: Daxamur WAN 2.2 FLF2V (v12.1)
workflows.description: Imported from a user-authored ComfyUI export (daxamursWAN22WorkflowsV121FLF2VT2V_flf2vV121.zip / Daxamur_WAN22_FLF2V_12.1.json), preserved as-is: a first-last-frame-to-video Wan 2.2 14B pipeline with a two-pass "motion" + "detail" KSamplerAdvanced chain, NAG (Normalized Attention Guidance) and CFG Zero Star conditioning, SageAttention patching, optional RealESRGAN upscale and RIFE frame interpolation stages (each individually bypassable via rgthree Fast Groups Bypasser), all wired through rgthree Set/Get nodes instead of direct links. The two UNETLoaders pointed at Kijai's repackaged Wan2_2-I2V-A14B-HIGH/LOW_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors, which aren't installed under those names in this suite - repointed to this suite's wan2.2_i2v_high/low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors, which are the same underlying models. Both LoraLoaderModelOnly nodes referenced the same Wan21_I2V_14B_lightx2v_cfg_step_distill_lora_rank64.safetensors for the high- and low-noise passes - repointed to the installed lightx2v_I2V_14B_480p_cfg_step_distill_rank64_bf16.safetensors, which is the same lightx2v cfg-step-distillation LoRA and preserves the source graph's one-file-for-both-passes design. Two models could not be resolved to an installed equivalent and are left pointing at their original filenames with a download url in this manifest: the CLIPVisionLoader's clip-vit-large-patch14.safetensors (OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14 vision encoder feeding the FLF2V image conditioning - substituting the installed sigclip/dino_v3 vision encoders would silently break it, since they use different embedding dimensions) and the UpscaleModelLoader's RealESRGAN_x2plus.pth (the installed RealESRGAN_x4plus.safetensors is a 4x model, not the 2x model the graph's resolution-multiplier math is built around, so it isn't a safe drop-in - the optional upscale stage is bypassed by default via the Fast Groups Bypasser). Beyond core ComfyUI, this graph depends on ComfyUI-KJNodes (PathchSageAttentionKJ, CFGZeroStarAndInit, WanVideoNAG, SomethingToString), rgthree-comfy (Set/Get Node, Power Lora Loader, Fast Groups Bypasser), ComfyUI_essentials (ImageRemoveAlpha+), ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation (RIFE VFI), ComfyUI-Easy-Use (easy int/easy seed/easy mathInt), and M1kep/ComfyLiterals (the plain Int/Float literal nodes used throughout for FPS/steps/CFG math) - none of which were installed, so they were cloned from their well-known upstream GitHub repos following the same deps-in-workflow resolution approach as the other imported packs. It also uses Daxamur/DaxNodes (the workflow author's own small utility pack, also cloned) for ResolutionPickerFLF2V. One remaining gap: a "String to Float" utility node (used only for internal FPS display-string math, not for anything model-related) has cnr_id "cg-image-filter" in the export, but that pack's current release registers the equivalent node as "cg_String to Float" rather than "String to Float" - an upstream rename since this workflow was authored. cg-image-filter is installed, but ComfyUI may still list this one node as missing until it's manually swapped for the pack's current "cg_String to Float" node.

workflows.name: Flexible Inpaint (Uncensored)
workflows.description: Mask-based inpainting for when the Juggernaut XL-based object-removal/repair workflows refuse a prompt. Paint the area to edit as a white region on a black mask image, describe what should appear there, and this graph encodes only that region, samples it, and composites the result back onto the untouched source pixels. Defaults to the Reed XXX Illustrious checkpoint (an uncensored SDXL finetune already used by the community-models pack) instead of Juggernaut XL, but the checkpoint field can be swapped to any installed SDXL checkpoint.

inputs.label: Checkpoint
inputs.description: SDXL checkpoint to sample with. Swap this if a given finetune still refuses a prompt.

inputs.label: Mask image
inputs.description: Black/white mask (paint the edit region white, everything else black)

inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.default: masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, seamlessly blended edit, natural lighting and texture matching the surrounding photo
inputs.description: Describe what should appear in the masked region

inputs.label: Negative prompt
inputs.default: visible seam, mismatched lighting, blurry, low quality, watermark, extra limbs, bad anatomy

inputs.label: Mask feather (px)
inputs.description: Grows/softens the mask edge so the composite blends in

inputs.label: Denoise
inputs.description: How strongly to redraw the masked region (1.0 = ignore the source content entirely)

outputs.description: Source image with only the masked region redrawn

workflows.name: Cocoamix (Qwen-Image-Edit LoRA)
workflows.description: Pairs the cocoamixQIedit.safetensors LoRA with the Qwen-Image-Edit base already installed in this suite (qwen_image_edit_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors, qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors, qwen_image_vae.safetensors - all present under those exact names, no substitutions needed). Built as a clean, minimal graph rather than reusing the legacy studio-migrated qwen-edit pack's flattened subgraph-derived node IDs: LoadImage -> ImageScaleToTotalPixels -> VAEEncode (for the sampler's starting latent) and, in parallel, into TextEncodeQwenImageEdit as the edit-reference image (Qwen-Image-Edit conditions on a reference latent attached to the positive conditioning rather than doing classic partial-denoise img2img, hence full denoise=1 from a real, image-derived latent) -> UNETLoader -> LoraLoaderModelOnly (cocoamix) -> ModelSamplingAuraFlow -> CFGNorm -> KSampler -> VAEDecode -> SaveImage. The ModelSamplingAuraFlow shift (3.0), CFGNorm inclusion, and 20-step/cfg-2.5 sampling settings are taken from ComfyUI's own bundled Qwen-Image-Edit reference template (comfyui_workflow_templates_json/templates/image_qwen_image_edit.json) rather than guessed, using its "comfy" (non-lightning-LoRA) settings row since we're loading the cocoamix style LoRA in that slot instead of a speed-distillation LoRA.

inputs.label: Edit instruction
inputs.default: Change the outfit to a red dress

workflows.name: Anima Inpaint (v1 Beta, PotatCats)
workflows.description: Imported from a user-authored ComfyUI export (comfyuiInpaintWorkflow_animaV1Beta/PotatCats-inpaint_ workflow-ANIMA-V1Beta-rel.json), preserved as-is: mask-based segment inpainting over the Anima architecture, with automatic segment cropping, growth/blur, and color-matched compositing back onto the source image. The original UNETLoader pointed at anima-base-v1.0.safetensors, which was never installed in this suite — repointed to the Anima Aesthetic v1.1 checkpoint used as the default Anima base elsewhere in this suite. Beyond core ComfyUI, rgthree-comfy, and Impact-Pack, this graph depends on ComfyUI-KJNodes (ColorMatchV2), ComfyI2I (Inpaint Segments, GrowMaskWithBlur), Comfyroll CustomNodes (CR Color Panel), masquerade-nodes-comfyui (Cut By Mask, Combine and Paste), and ComfyUI-Cosmos-Reference (ApplyCosmosReferenceLatent) — all resolved via ComfyUI-Manager's deps-in-workflow against this file and installed.

inputs.label: Negative prompt
inputs.default: jpeg artifacts, lowres, worst quality, low quality, bad hands
